detours.why: D-666 ARM B: this B.Cu segment TERMINATES at the barrel (59.300,106.300) the same spec removes.  Relaying it between its own two ends asks the router to reach a site that is reserved and a bond that is gone; ARM A asked exactly that and got NO_PATH at 0.300 mm inside a 5.180 mm budget.  It is a stub of a removed bond, so it is REMOVED AND NOT PUT BACK and the gate's inert_removal_priced clause prices it.

note: D-667 ARM F -- the promotable shape.  Same EIGHT physical units as D-666 arms A-E and the same stated max_mm as arm E (15.0 / 12.0 mm).  TWO things are different and both are framework, not geometry.  (1) THE LANE IS PER-LAYER: evidence/d667-wake-lane-perlayer.json reserves each of arm C's six route segments on the ONE layer that segment occupies -- F, B, In2, F, In2, B -- plus a 0.500 mm all-layer disc at each of the five barrel sites, 31.187 mm against D-666's 93.561 mm.  A route occupies one layer between two of its barrels and the other two layers are the only way a net it evicted can ever cross it; D-666 reserved all three for the whole length and measured the consequence as NO_PATH on both relays.  (2) THE RELAY'S OWN ENDS ARE LIFTED: a reservation reaches keepout + width/2 + G = 0.450 mm where the DRC-legal separation of two 0.200 mm tracks at 0.200 mm clearance is 0.400 mm, so it swallows the terminals of the very copper the lane's route displaced.  evidence/d667-terminal-lift-probe.json measures it: /IR_TX_GPIO16's goal cell at (56.950,109.700) and /SX1262_CS_N's at (58.4242,111.2007) each had ZERO of 24 free neighbours on ALL THREE reserved layers -- the wave had a seed and nowhere to go, at any budget.  route_maze_batch.terminal_lift frees exactly the guard's own reach at each fixed end, on that end's OWN layer only, and reports what it freed on the detour's record.
